name: First Abu Dhabi Bank
founded: 2017 (merger of National Bank of Abu Dhabi and First Gulf Bank; current board members appointed from 31 Mar 2017)
ownership_summary: Listed on ADX. At 30 Jun 2026 FAB reported its shareholders as Mubadala Investment Company 37.9%, Abu Dhabi Ruling Family 17.7%, other UAE entities/individuals 20.0% and foreign investors 24.4% (foreign ownership limit 40%). The Chairman is H.H. Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Ruler of Abu Dhabi.
government_link: Yes. Mubadala Investment Company (Abu Dhabi sovereign investor) holds 37.9% and the Abu Dhabi Ruling Family 17.7% (30 Jun 2026); Chairman is the Deputy Ruler of Abu Dhabi (board page checked 2026-10-12).
group_structure: Group parent First Abu Dhabi Bank PJSC (Abu Dhabi PJSC). Four reporting segments since a 2025 reorganisation: Investment Banking & Markets (IB&M), Wholesale Banking (WB), Personal, Business, Wealth & Privileged Client Banking Group (PBW&PCBG) and Head Office. Wealth-relevant subsidiaries (100% unless stated, 30 Jun 2026): First Abu Dhabi Bank Securities (UAE brokerage), FAB Private Bank (Suisse) SA (Switzerland), First Abu Dhabi Islamic Finance PJSC, FAB Asset Management Limited (ADGM, FSRA-authorised 22 May 2026), FAB Capital Financial Company (KSA), First Abu Dhabi Bank Misr (Egypt). Associates include Neptune Project Holding 1 (34%, payment services), Nebras Open Finance (15%), AEDC Stable Coin entities (33%, new in 2026) and Global Climate Finance Centre (44%). Wio Bank (profiled separately as ae-wio) is not among FAB's consolidated subsidiaries or associates; FAB's Group Head of PBW&PCBG sits on Wio's board. No double counting: all metrics below are FAB group consolidated.

footprint: 20+ markets across 5 continents and 140+ branches globally (30 Jun 2026, S8); the CEO biography says 22 markets (S2). International franchise contributed 22% of H1 2026 revenue; international assets AED 437bn, 31% of group assets (S6). FS list operations in the UAE, Bahrain, Brazil, Cayman Islands, China, Egypt, France, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Iraq, Jordan, KSA, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Malaysia, Nigeria, Oman, Qatar, Singapore, South Korea, Switzerland, Turkey, UK and USA (S4).
customer_segments: Retail and SME (Personal and Business Banking), affluent (FAB Elite, 10 Elite Centres), HNW/UHNW and family offices (Private Banking, incl. Switzerland, KSA, Singapore, UK, France), privileged clients, large and mid corporates (Wholesale Banking), institutional and public-sector clients (IB&M).
business_lines: PBW&PCBG (H1 2026 operating income AED 6,583m) combines retail, Elite, private banking, privileged client and SME banking, offering 'retail banking, private banking and tailored investment and advisory solutions' (S4 note 30). Wealth products: investment advisory, discretionary portfolio management (conventional and Shariah mandates), trade execution in bonds/equities/FX and proprietary and third-party funds, Lombard and real-estate lending, wealth planning and trust services (S17); FAB Funds and global third-party funds, structured products, custody in 70+ markets and securities brokerage (S18). FAB Securities provides brokerage on ADX, DFM and Nasdaq Dubai via FABS Online and the FAB Securities app (S12). IB&M and Wholesale Banking cover institutional, public-sector and corporate clients.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Wealth sits in the Personal, Business, Wealth & Privileged Client Banking Group led by Futoon Al Mazrouei since 2025 (H1 2026 operating income AED 6.58bn, +2% yoy; non-interest income -16% yoy). FAB reports 'retail AUMs' up 20% yoy in H1 2026 but discloses no AUM figure. Affluent clients are served through FAB Elite (10 Elite Centres, RM and wealth specialists, advisory and portfolio reviews) and HNW clients through FAB Private Banking in the UAE, Switzerland (FAB Private Bank (Suisse) SA), KSA, Singapore, UK and France, offering advisory, discretionary mandates (conventional or Shariah), trade execution and Lombard lending. Product shelf includes FAB Funds, unnamed third-party funds and structured products; FAB signed product partnerships with Amundi (Dec 2025) and T. Rowe Price (Jan 2026) for retail, private banking and institutional clients. A new ADGM asset manager, FAB Asset Management Limited, was authorised on 22 May 2026 (no retail clients). Digital investing in FAB Mobile is limited to opening a FAB trading account, investor numbers, IPO subscriptions and portfolio tracking; FAB Securities' app trades ADX, DFM and Nasdaq Dubai. The Group Head of Global Private Banking (Michel Longhini) left in early 2026 and no successor was found.

asset_management.detail: FAB Funds ('award winning investment funds' in equities and fixed income) run by the bank's Investment Management team (S18). FAB Asset Management Limited (ADGM, FSP 250064, authorised 22 May 2026): Managing Assets, Managing a Collective Investment Fund, Advising, Arranging Deals, Arranging Custody, Islamic Financial Business; not permitted to deal with retail clients or hold client assets (S20). 'FAB Asset Management' manages the FAB End of Service Benefit funds (conventional and Islamic, capital-protected) under the MOHRE/SCA savings scheme (S19). AUM not disclosed.

brokerage.detail: First Abu Dhabi Bank Securities (100%): execution, research (UAE and regional equity and fixed income) and custody; FABS Online web platform and FAB Securities mobile app with direct market access to ADX and DFM; markets named: ADX, DFM, Nasdaq Dubai (S12). Private-bank trade execution covers bonds, equities, FX and funds (S17).

digital_investing.detail: Limited. FAB Mobile (Elite promotion page, 2026): open a FAB trading account, apply for ADX/DFM National Investor Number, early access to regional IPO subscriptions, daily/monthly portfolio statements (S15). Separate FAB Securities app for ADX/DFM/Nasdaq Dubai trading (S12). No in-app global equities, funds or model portfolios found (S15, S18).

advisory.detail: Elite: investment advisory, portfolio solutions and reviews, wealth planning (S14). Private Banking: global investment advisory across asset classes (S17).

discretionary.detail: Private Banking discretionary portfolio management with 'conventional or Shariah-compliant mandates across asset classes, geographies and investment profiles' (S17).

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisory or model-portfolio product found on the Elite, Private Banking, Invest or mobile pages (S13–S18). FAB Invest page shows six risk profiles but links to savings pages (S18).

funds_platform.detail: 'Global (Third Party) Funds' with 'privileged access to best of breed fund managers' (managers not named) and FAB Funds (S18); private-bank trade execution in 'proprietary and third-party funds' (S17). Platform provider not named. Product partnerships signed with Amundi (Dec 2025) and T. Rowe Price (Jan 2026) (S21, S22).

structured_products.detail: Listed on the personal Invest page: 'Designed so that you can capitalise on market opportunities while protecting you from risks' (S18). Issuers not named.

private_markets.detail: No named private-markets product for wealth clients found. The T. Rowe Price partnership (Jan 2026) covers equity, fixed income, alternatives and multi-asset, and its CEO refers to solutions 'across public and private markets' to be jointly developed (S21). Private Banking mentions real-estate 'unique investment opportunities' (S17).

islamic_wealth.detail: Shariah-compliant discretionary mandates and Shariah-compliant lending in Private Banking (S17); Elite Islamic proposition (S13); FAB Islamic End of Service Benefit Fund (S19); FAB Asset Management Limited holds an FSRA Islamic Financial Business permission (S20).

opportunities: Building out its investment shelf with global managers: Amundi (Dec 2025) and T. Rowe Price (Jan 2026) partnerships for retail, private banking and institutional clients, with T. Rowe Price to 'jointly develop and launch new solutions' incl. alternatives (S21, S22).
Retail AUMs grew 20% yoy in H1 2026, yet PBW&PCBG non-interest income fell 16% yoy to AED 1,668m (S6, S7).
Investment fee pool is small for the bank's size: 'asset management and investment services' fee income AED 199m and brokerage income AED 155m in FY2025, against total fee income of AED 7,057m (S5).

Digital investing is thin: FAB Mobile offers trading-account opening, investor numbers, IPO subscriptions and portfolio tracking; FAB Securities app covers ADX, DFM and Nasdaq Dubai only; no in-app global equities, funds or model portfolios found (S12, S15, S18).
No robo/model-portfolio proposition found; Elite and Private Banking eligibility not published (S13, S14, S17, S18).

Group-wide AI push (Copilot for all staff, 4,800+ agents, 150+ use cases) but no client-facing or RM wealth AI tool evidenced (S9).
Group Head of Global Private Banking post vacated in early 2026; successor not found (S1, S26).
barriers: Large in-house technology and transformation organisation under a Group CTTO (ex-Standard Chartered); AI Innovation Hub with 60+ specialists (S2, S9).
